name: Studio reference

source.reference: Authored Automatron demonstration system; not Alps or a third-party brand

principles: Minimum reading, maximum clarity. Remove repetitive explanation before content, controls, or consequences.
Compose around the object and the task. A gallery, document, and work list should have different structures.
Use one dominant action for the current task; retain meaningful secondary actions nearby.
Use imagery and scale for orientation. No decorative card grids or repeated heading-description-button stacks by default.
Remove repeated headings, numbered wrappers, helper paragraphs, and implementation labels already explained by the visual. Avoid em dashes and en dashes in product copy.
For a cinematic demonstration, make motion explain the trigger and outcome. Provide pause and replay for loops, honor reduced motion, and suspend hidden playback.
Keep unfamiliar actions labelled. Preserve keyboard access, visible focus, readable contrast, and reduced-motion alternatives.
This reference system uses a dark editorial shell, a single accent, and strong typographic contrast. Other brands retain their own direction.

rules: Make the document the dominant object and keep the decision facts beside it.
Use scale, spacing and alignment instead of dividers, decorative summary cards or repeated totals.
Reserve the accent for the single primary action.
Keep supplier, amount, due date, destination and consequence visible at the decision point.
Let the source draft and result carry the explanation; no headline, captions or tutorial copy in the stage.
Keep model labels under each other in a stable rail. Show one source at a time at full size.
Sweep a scan across the source, then cut to the result; two source screens are never composited on screen.
Keep the composed result identical across sources; the source changes, the result does not.
Use one accent for the result's primary action; keep source drafts in their own generic palettes. Keep the header, rail and primary action free of decorative badges, icons and arrows.
Disclose authored sources and simulations in optional details.

font.display.value: Iowan Old Style, Palatino, Georgia, serif

components.name: Button
rules: Use a visible action label.
Only the current primary action receives data-primary.

components.name: IconButton
rules: Provide an accessible name and a 44px target.
Only use for familiar actions.

components.name: SegmentedControl
rules: Name the group and expose aria-pressed.

components.name: Poster
rules: Keep title and availability readable over artwork.
Artwork is decorative when title supplies identity.

components.name: Field
rules: Keep a visible associated label.
A placeholder is not a label.

components.name: Dialog
rules: Use native dialog.showModal(), Escape dismissal, and restore focus.

components.name: Status
rules: Pair color with a text status.

components.name: TaskRow
rules: Use a labelled native checkbox.
Retain owner and due date.

components.name: Receipt
rules: Show itemization and totals.
All demonstration values are fixtures.

components.name: PaymentSummary
rules: Show supplier, amount, due date, destination and consequence at the decision point.
Keep one primary action. Do not add a second summary card that repeats the same facts.
Keep the consequence visible in the confirmation state.

components.name: EmptyState
rules: State what happened and provide a meaningful recovery action.
